body: Rules as described by Druckenmiller in interviews: (1) Earnings don't move the overall market; central banks and liquidity do - focus on the Fed (for India: RBI stance, system liquidity, FPI flows, the rupee and US real yields). (2) Look 18-24 months ahead; price action today reflects what investors expect then. (3) When several signals line up (liquidity, valuation, technicals/price confirmation), bet big - concentration, not diversification, is where returns come from. (4) Use price as information: if the market doesn't confirm the thesis, cut fast; preservation of capital comes first. (5) Change your mind without ego when the regime changes. Individual adaptation: a quarterly liquidity checklist (RBI repo direction, banking-system liquidity surplus/deficit, credit growth, FPI and DII flows, USD/INR trend) to tilt equity exposure; fewer, larger positions with explicit exit conditions. Failure mode: overconfidence and chasing at the top (his own 2000 tech buy). Evidence: his record is press-reported, not audited; treat this as a process template, not a proven formula for individuals.
title: Druckenmiller: liquidity-first, concentrated macro
